Base Mercedes-AMG GT SUV Receives CGI Pure Stock Treatment: Black Plastics, Steelies, Manual Windows
8 photos
Photo: kelsonik / Instagram
The 2027 Mercedes-AMG GT SUV , which has a dedicated EV architecture and no correspondent in the Mercedes-Benz family, is the 2027 Mercedes-AMG GT 4-Door Coupe’s high riding sibling, and they show major similarities while being rather unique propositions on the automotive market – arriving sometime in 2027.
The automotive world is going to extremes as of late: some carmakers are going back to the roots of affordability with base models like the Citroen 2CV concept seen recently at the 2026 Paris Motor Show, while others only seem to think that the most powerful and exclusive vehicles matter nowadays.
The roster of such models includes things like the Mercedes- AMG GT 4-Door Coupe, or the Ferrari Luce and the newly introduced Jaguar Type 01, recently. Actually, Mercedes is doubling the gamble with the newly introduced GT SUV, too, which is a high-performance model for the high-end. Kind of like the new Bentley Torcal, but with a focus on sportiness rather than outright opulence. Well, if you’re not into six-figure automobiles and would rather see the carmakers go back to making affordable, attainable models, no worries – there’s a solution.
Albeit it comes from the parallel universes of vehicular CGI thanks to a member of the imaginative guild of digital car content creators. More precisely, Nikita Chuicko, the virtual artist better known as " kelsonik " on social media, thinks that now is the right CGI time to work on the new 2027 Mercedes-AMG GT SUV and included it in his new series of CGI ‘Pure Stock’ models.
The latter also includes the Jaguar Type 01, the all-new G50 BMW 3 Series, the Bentley Torcal all-electric crossover ultra-SUV, the latest Audi Q7, or the G65 BMW X5 and iX5, among others. The pixel master probably started the series as an experiment, but since it has become quite successful, he continues to morph the latest novelties from controversial experiments into ‘mundane’ models that anyone could probably afford due to the cost-cutting measures.
More precisely, the new Mercedes-AMG GT SUV gets dressed in a base , non-metallic white hue, adopts a simpler front fascia with black plastic radiator grilles and a basic bumper, has black plastic protection elements all around the lower parts of the body, and also mixes steel wheels with simple roof rails and a cheap rear diffuser.
The author does keep the hidden door handles and paints the exterior mirrors, as this is a premium model, after all (sic). Moving inside, the situation is even more hilarious: the triple-screen setup has disappeared in favor of separate small-sized displays for the instrument cluster and the infotainment system, for example.
Additionally, the three dials on the central tunnel are now up on the dashboard as manual controls for the AC, and all the upholstery elements are plain and simple gray cloth. There are still some premium touches like the steering wheel and the carbon fiber on the door handles or the center tunnel, but even the front windows now have hand cranks! Photo: JNPA
By Angelo Mathais India correspondent
26 October 2026
Rates for containers moving from China to India have begun to cool as seasonal import demand, associated with India’s festival-driven consumption, loses momentum.
New data secured by The Loadstar points to a 10%-20% decline in spot rates for bookings from major Chinese load ports to India, particularly JNPA (Nhava Sheva) on the west coast and Chennai on the east.
For example, Indian importers are now able to book a 40ft shipment from Shanghai to JNPA at about $3,200 per box, down from about $3,800 a month ago. Likewise, rates ex-Shanghai to Chennai have dropped to $3,200 per 40ft from $3,900.
Ocean rates from other Asian hubs like Hong Kong and Singapore to India have also begun to trend down, after remaining elevated over the past two months, according to the data.
Hong Kong-JNPA rates are currently in the region of $3,600/40ft, down from $3,800 a month ago, while carriers are booking freight from Singapore to JNPA at about $3,400/40ft, 5% lower than in September.
Spot rates from Hong Kong to Chennai have fallen 15%, to $3,300/40ft, the data indicates.
But executives at leading intra-Asia carriers claimed the latest moderate correction should not be seen as the onset of a broader cyclical downturn as, according to them, trades from Asia to India and the Middle East still remained caught up in port challenges and delays across the region.
“Our Asia-India-Middle East vessels continue to operate under a lot of operational strain on the Persian Gulf end,” one source told The Loadstar. “Delays at Khor Fakkan are not getting any better.”
Amid sliding sailing schedules for Asian services, vessel bunching added considerable berthing window pressure at JNPA recently.
However, India-China trade indicators are bullish. According to available data, Indian imports from China, by value, saw a meteoric rise in the first three quarters this year, up 23% year on year, underscoring the strength of trade flows that had helped propel the resurgent demand for container shipping.
While trade between India and China has historically favoured Beijing by a massive margin, India’s exports to China have gained measurable pace in the past few years as a result of accelerated bilateral negotiations. The rebalancing has also provided regional carriers with reasonably better cargo yields on the backhaul.
Freight from India for intra-Asia operators in the past had been in negative territory, often involving $5 per container for insurance coverage.
The demand boom has also driven an influx of fresh capacity into the tradelane, mainly connecting intra-Asia markets into JNPA and Chennai in recent months.
India’s overall export trade outlook has significantly strengthened in recent months, despite the supply chain turmoil plaguing major trade routes. According to provisional data, India’s fiscal year 2026-27 H1 exports, by value, were up 18.5% year on year, growth mainly driven by electronics, engineering goods, chemicals, and agricultural products.
“The strength of the first-half performance lies in the diversity of its growth drivers,” said SC Ralhan, president of the Federation of Indian Export Organisations.
“Sustaining this balance, while expanding our market reach, will be crucial in the second half of the financial year,” he added.

White C8 Chevy Corvette ZR1 Drags Blue Ford Mustang Shelby GT500, Someone Should Have Stayed Home
13 photos
Photo: Wheels / YouTube
The videographer behind the ' Wheels ' channel on YouTube recently took a detour around BMP – aka Bradenton Motorsports Park in Florida for some cool excerpts from the FL2K competition, then headed back to one of its favorite venues. Well, now they’re back at BMP, most likely because they remembered they had this feisty encounter lying around the editing room…
This videographer is very passionate about a couple of racing tracks in North America: one is the iconic The Strip at Las Vegas Motor Speedway , which is among the very few in the country with a four-lane arrangement. The other one is MRP – aka Mission Raceway Park or Thunder by the River – which is an auto racing facility located in Mission, British Columbia, Canada, with an NHRA-sanctioned quarter-mile dragstrip.
But just recently the videographer decided to add a third track on its repertoire, the legendary Bradenton Motorsports Park in Florida , as they showed us excerpts from the cool FL2K competition, an event which gathered “the southeast’s fastest street cars.” We have seen quite a bunch of interesting skirmishes, and we’re glad the videographer also remembered about this one.
That’s because it’s a classic General Motors versus the Ford Motor Company encounter, albeit slightly novel in its format because the traditional S550 Ford Mustang Shelby GT500 muscle car, equipped with the 5.2-liter supercharged Predator V8, got into a battle with the modern C8 Chevrolet Corvette in one of its top configurations, the 1,064-horsepower ZR1 packing the brand-new 5.5-liter twin-turbo V8 behind the seats and a mid-engine configuration.
Normally, the Shelby GT500 is a mid-ten to low-elevens car, depending on the in stock condition, depending on the surface, tires, and testing conditions; while GM says the latest ZR1 can do better than that, somewhere in the mid- to high nines depending on the track, tires, and weather. But, of course, either the blue Shelby GT500 or the white C8 ZR1 or both could be modified.
Well, it’s safe to say that the human factor is also very important, as the Corvette driver launched better than its adversary and had a car-length advantage while passing the Christmas tree, but something happened afterward and the pursuing Shelby GT500 made a spectacular comeback to catch up and defeat its adversary with a 9.34s pass at 137 mph, while the ZR1 only achieved a 10.04s pass at a much lower trap speed of less than 125 mph.
If anyone wonders what happened with the one driver that should have stayed home instead of getting ashamed, the comments section, as always, has a ton of opinions about who’s best and what’s better – GM or Ford’s ride. So, what do you think happened there – did the C8 driver get cold feet when achieving the high speed, or got scared by the roaring Shelby coming back to win the skirmish?

When it’s time for commercial flooring to be replaced, renovation teams may be inclined to toss it in the dumpster along with other construction and demolition debris, but Shaw Industries wants its EcoWorx carpet tile back.
The reverse logistics challenge
Getting that product back to the company so it can be recycled into new flooring is an exercise in sophisticated reverse logistics and effective use of freight. It comes off the floor seven to 10 years after delivery, often in small lots. By then the owner or tenant may have changed and not be aware that the flooring is recyclable or know who manufactured the product.
To combat this challenge, the Dalton, Ga., flooring maker has implemented a number of steps to make it easier for that product to be returned to Shaw rather than ending up in a landfill. For years, the company has printed a toll-free number and URL on the back of its EcoWorx carpet tile, which launched in 1999, so that demolition teams knows who to contact for product takeback.
“We also have tools within our own operations where we can identify places that we know we have had our products installed,” said Candi Hampton, vice president of global sustainability at Shaw, in an interview with FreightWaves. “That allows Shaw team members to contact them when they’re likely getting ready for renovation to ensure they are aware of our reclamation and recycling services, which are available at no cost to the customer.”
Shaw often needed a full truck or a substantial amount on a truck for it to be cost-effective to bring it back to the company.
Shaw’s answer, worked out in 2022 and 2023, was to run returns through the regional distribution centers that handle its outbound deliveries. Doing so allowed the company to collect smaller quantities from its customers and store it at the distribution center until enough material is collected to transport it to the company’s manufacturing and recycling facility in northwest Georgia. In a November 2023 release, the company cut the minimum for a no-charge EcoWorx pickup in the U.S. under its re[TURN] Reclamation Program from 500 square yards to 100.
The lower minimum fits a market where commercial spaces have shrunk, Hampton said, and floors now mix carpet with hard surfaces and unfinished or polished concrete.
Returns ride the outbound network
Shaw makes 2,700 customer deliveries a day and reaches 99% of the U.S. population in two days or less, according to the company’s supply chain and logistics page . The November 2023 release put its count of regional distribution centers at 30. Shaw ranks 75th on Transport Topics’ 2026 Top 100 Private Carriers list , with 689 tractors and 3,191 trailers.
That network is built around delivery dates. “If you’re building a house and trying to close, it needs to be there on time,” said Sara Martin, Shaw’s vice president of corporate marketing and communications, in a separate interview.
Most of Shaw’s truckload freight moves between its major hubs and its regional distribution centers, FreightWaves noted back in 2021 . The regional centers also run local trucks that go back and forth to customers.
Those local trucks now pick up reclaimed carpet tile from customers, and customers near a center can drop it off themselves. Pickup sites still need room for a 53-foot trailer and a live load , under Shaw’s reclamation program guidelines .
“That allows us to consolidate different projects so that we have a larger footprint to then bring back to Georgia on a truck that was coming back empty anyways,” Hampton said.
Shaw still uses a couple of third-party partners where no regional center is close by, but Hampton said the distribution centers are the main route because they are more cost-effective.
Back into the backing
Once a load reaches Georgia, the tile goes into a process that chops it up, melts it and turns it into pellets. Those pellets are blended with other compounded pellets to make new backing. Shaw used to separate the fiber from the backing and use each differently.
“We’ve been able to change that process so that now everything goes into the backing, and we’re able to recycle 100% of that carpet tile back into the backing,” Hampton said.
Hampton said young Shaw engineers who had taken green chemistry classes in college built EcoWorx around principles Michael Braungart and William McDonough were promoting before Cradle to Cradle became a book or a product certification.
“If you design a product and you’re not thinking down the road what it might do at end of life, you likely don’t have very many options,” she said.
Since 2006, Shaw has reclaimed and recycled almost 1 billion pounds of carpet, including EcoWorx, according to the same release.
Recycling carpet tile counts toward a customer’s landfill diversion efforts, and using the recycled content in the manufacturing of a new carpet tile cuts its embodied carbon and the customer’s Scope 3 emissions.
Finding carpet tile installed years ago
Getting customers to send carpet tile back is the harder half. Hampton did not have a return rate to share and said it can be challenging. “There is a lot of miseducation and misperception out there,” she said.
“These products are going down. It might be seven, might be 10 years before the products are coming back up,” Hampton said. “And so the owners may have changed, the end users may have changed. They might not actually know.”
Specifications are one fix. Shaw works with architects and designers to write reclamation into product and building specs, so the instruction is on paper when the tile comes up, Hampton said.
Landfill fees decide where tile comes back
Where carpet tile and other flooring comes back from often depends on what it costs to throw it away. While recycling supports customers’ sustainability priorities, Hampton said returns come easiest where landfills charge high tipping fees: California, New York, Massachusetts and Seattle.
“Places that don’t have massive tipping fees, like Alabama or Mississippi, are harder places to get our products back,” she said.
The contractor tearing out the floor decides where the flooring goes.
“A lot of times they think it’s going to be too hard or too expensive, or it’s just so much easier to throw everything they’re demoing into a single dumpster instead of having to segregate,” she said.
Shaw has hired sustainability specialists for the Seattle and Boston areas and just added one in Dallas. Along with architects and designers, they go directly to contractors and demolition contractors, who aren’t typically the customer Shaw is engaged with when selling its products.
“So being able to have those people that can connect directly to the contractors or the demo contractors, take them step-by-step through the process, walk the space with them, really educate them, has made a huge improvement in our efforts to get product back,” Hampton said.

All-New 2028 Cadillac Escalade PHEV Gains Deep Facelift Along With Plug-in Hybrid Setup – Rendering
21 photos
Photo: AutoYa / YouTube
General Motors has recently announced that it is looking forward to engineering the “intelligence-defined vehicle for everyone,” as GM is joining the pack of automakers that are seeking “a fundamental transformation of our vehicles” as we know them.
GM will focus on a combination of AI, software-defined platforms, intelligent manufacturing, and trusted autonomous systems, with Cadillac at the forefront of the activities, of course. The premium brand needs attention, as sales have suffered because of its over-reliance on EVs, and the parent company now wants to help it gain back on the right course, with no expenses spared.
Even the OnStar service is going to be morphed into an AI assistant for the GM cars, especially Cadillacs at first, and the luxury brand is currently focused on its most popular model with ICE power in a bid to draw attention. For example, F1 driver Checo Perez got his own Escalade-V special edition, limited to just 11 examples, while the company also created the Escalade 125th Anniversary Collector Series with exclusive wheels, carbon fiber, and blue accents, among other things.
As such, perhaps it’s no surprise that even the rumor mill, along with the members of the imaginative guild of digital car content creators dwelling across the parallel universes of vehicular CGI, have thoughts about Cadillac in general and also about the Escalade in particular. More precisely, here are the good folks over at the " AutoYa " info channel on YouTube who have recently and unofficially imagined the CGI look of the potential all-new 2028 Cadillac Escalade PHEV for the US market.
The channel’s host believes that the upcoming sixth generation of the Cadillac Escalade might arrive in 2027 or 2028 because the current iteration has been around since 2020 and a mid-cycle refresh procedure was applied in 2024 for the 2025 model year. However, do take their assessment with a pinch of salt because Cadillac might simply apply a second refresh if they want to bring to market new features along with the fresh powertrain.
Speaking of the latter, the host believes that Cadillac will offer the first-ever plug-in hybrid powertrain based on a 1.5-liter four-cylinder turbo helped by two electric motors. However, that’s also rather unlikely, as GM won’t de-escalate the value of an Escalade with a four-cylinder. Instead, it would be plausible that one of the new V8 engines from the 2027 Chevy Silverado and GMC Sierra, the 5.7-liter or the 6.6-liter, could get an electrified setup to keep the Escalade’s elegance and power uncompromised.
Last but not least, the channel’s resident virtual artist quickly takes over to present the potential changes featured on the 2028 Cadillac Escalade PHEV, starting with a quick comparison with the current model to showcase the new visual identity, which includes a new front fascia and a reworked interior. Last but not least, they don’t forget about the traditional CGI color reel. So, what do you think – yay or nay?

New Dodge Hyper-Muscle Concept Wants To Steal the SRT Copperhead’s Thunder – Rendering
7 photos
Photo: Instagram | adry53customs
What’s the least exciting muscle car that money can buy today? Some might argue it’s the EcoBoost-powered S650 Ford Mustang , whereas other would say it is none other than the modern-day Dodge Charger.
Why the latter? Because while the former model can be specified with a V8 engine, the Charger cannot. And that’s despite the fact that it will blow two candles off its birthday cake at the end of the year. Production started in late 2024 at the Windsor factory in Ontario, Canada. Both body styles, the coupe and sedan, are based on the STLA Large (Longitudinal) platform, meaning that they share their nuts and bolts with the upcoming Stelvio and Giulia from Alfa Romeo, and the second-gen Maserati Levante.
But fret not, fellow gearhead, because while Dodge’s initial bet was on straight-six twin-turbocharged and electric firepower when it comes to the new-age Charger , the company admitted it was wrong not to launch this model with a V8. After all, multiple reviewers have said that it behaves like something that would feature a V8, and Dodge is now ready to take this step, with the rumor mill speaking about it hitting the assembly line at the end of 2027, and launching as a 2028 model year at dealers nationwide.
Hemi V8 firepower is therefore a thing, apparently, and word on the street is that it will be none other than the 6.2-liter supercharged V8 that might power this model. The Hellcat lump makes over 700 horsepower in its base configuration and more than 800 horsepower on superior models. And in its peak form, it offers 1,025 horsepower in the Dodge Challenger SRT Demon 170, rocketing it to 60 mph in 1.66 seconds, and turning it into an 8.91-second muscle car down the quarter mile, with an exit speed of over 151 mph (243+ kph).
Photo: Instagram | adry53customs Dodge has some bold ideas for its muscle car lineup, as the Copperhead is also in the making, reportedly. The model might get the SRT suffix in the top-of-the-line flavor, and was supposedly teased during the Stellantis Investor Day almost half a year ago, next to the GLH crossover that should utilize the STLA One platform, and could also get an SRT (or more) flavor.
The mysterious muscle car say under wraps in a teaser pic, and it looked very different from the standard Charger lineup. It looks like it has a big rear wing, so it would send Charger Daytona (the classic one, d’oh!) and Plymouth Superbird vibes. It will likely be based on the same platform as the modern-day Charger, and it should launch with V8 firepower, probably under the Dodge Copperhead (SRT) name.
Inspired by everything happening in Dodge’s upcoming lineup , the rendering crowd has already imagined quite a few monstrous-looking Charger-based muscle cars so far. One of the latest to have crossed our screens came from @adry63customs on Instagram. The pixel master dropped a short video of the so-called Dodge Hyper-Muscle Concept that shows it in motion from several angles, and while it is obviously on the very special side of things, it was clearly based on the modern-day Charger.
Photo: Instagram | adry53customs The CGI-infused study features a familiar front end, albeit a different bumper, and a very muscular-looking hood with a cutout for the supercharger. There wheel arches have been enlarged, the door mirrors are very slim, the back end is home to an intricate-looking diffuser and a ducktail spoiler, and we can also see that the big wheels are on the very special side of things.
But the icing on the cake lies beneath the skin, as something like this would have a dedicated chassis setup, as well as uprated brakes to keep the extra oomph in check. And the only firepower would be a V8 , with a supercharger assisting it. If we were to dream about it, we’d say that it deserves a four-digit output, though on a more realistic scenario, it would probably take on the Ford Mustang Dark Horse SC or, who knows, maybe the Mustang GTD.
This muscle car is one dark overall look away from tapping into its devilish side, and we’d say that the Hellcat decals on the rear three-quarter panels and rear pillars would be a welcomed addition. But let’s not forget that we are looking at a virtual study that lives its life in Fantasy Land, and has absolutely nothing in common with the upcoming V8-powered Dodge Charger, which is expected for the 2028 model year as mentioned above, nor the Copperhead, that could be due in 2029 or perhaps 2030.
Now, this CGI model’s overall design is definitely not bad at all, but to be honest, it is not perfect either, as it is a bit on the flashy side of things. But assuming this is what the V8-powered Charger would look like, would you order one over an S650 Ford Mustang with an eight-cylinder engine under the hood? Aprilia RS 660 Phillip Island Is the Italian Way of Saying Goodbye to the Historic Track
7 photos
Photo: Aprilia
Nestled on a small piece of land located some 78 miles (125 km) off the coast of Melbourne, Australia, the Phillip Island Circuit has been for years one of the most important race tracks in the world. Over the decades, it was home to the Australian GP, World Superbikes races, V8 supercars show-offs, you name it.
The place has also been home to the MotoGP series, hosting one leg of one of the most interesting motorcycle racing series in the world over the past 28 years or so. That will change, though, as, citing a variety of reasons, from weather conditions to the need to modernize the track, MotoGP is moving from Phillip Island starting next season.
The final Grand Prix of the series there was supposed to take place this past weekend, but it was cancelled on account of weather and visibility issues. This kind of robbed those who wanted the bid the proper farewell to the track of their opportunity to do so.
As one of the bike makers that have made history over the years at Phillip Island, Italian bike maker Aprilia presented in the week that preceded the now-cancelled last race on the track a special edition of its RS 660 mid-range sports bike.
Officially called the Aprilia RS 660 Phillip Island Tribute, the bike comes with unique graphics and equipment, carefully selected and tailored in such a way as to not only honor the circuit, but also to remind people of what the place meant for Aprilia.
Photo: Aprilia Over on the remote island, the bike maker secured over the years ten victories across the various classes of the MotoGP World Championship, and a number of wins in the Superbike World Championship.
It is also the place where, back in 2025, rider Raul Fernandez rode the RS-GP motorcycle to the win in MotoGP, marking Aprilia's 300th win in the World Motorcycle Championship and making the brand the most successful European manufacturer in the history of the event.
The Aprilia RS 660 Phillip Island Tribute carries all that history on its bodywork, starting with the dedicated livery and ending with the side panels that carry, as a sort of permanent tattoo, the circuit’s logo formed by the track layout, the words Phillip Island Circuit, and the chequered flag at the finish line.
Built on a bike whose base color is white, the Tribute features green on the sides and tail section and red on the wheel rims as a means to highlight the colors of the circuit's logos. The badge on the fuel tank is there to remind everyone of the number of victories Aprilia scored at Phillip Island over the years.
Photo: Aprilia The bike also comes equipped with a passenger seat cover included as standard, and there is a serial number inscribed on the steering head plate.
Mechanically speaking, the Phillip Island Tribute is not different from the RS 660 it is based on. That means its frame holds the standard 660cc four-valve, front-mounted twin-cylinder engine, capable of developing 105 hp at 10,400 rpm and 70 Nm of torque at 8,400 rpm.
Just like in the rest of the range, the engine acts as a load-bearing element for the motorcycle and is controlled by means of a bidirectional electronic transmission.
The Tribute also carries over the many technologies that are packed into the production version, including traction control, wheelie control, engine braking control, cornering ABS and engine mapping, controlled via the electronic throttle control.
Photo: Aprilia Aprilia did not say how many of these bikes it will make, or how much one of them will cost. It did say, however, that it would be bringing the two-wheeler to the Esposizione Internazionale Ciclo Motociclo e Accessori (EICMA) show in Milan, Italy, which opens its doors early next month. autoevolution will be on location, and we'll send word on availability and pricing if and when Aprilia reveals them.
As for the Australian Grand Prix for next year's MotoGP season, even if Phillip Island falls off the calendar, the race will still be held. The track that will replace the Island is the one in Adelaide.
Unveiled in the summer of this year, the local circuit will become home to the world's first city-center MotoGP race to come to life, as it will unfold itself on the city's streets. The new circuit stretches for 2.56 miles (4.13 km) and comes with 15 corners.
The track is a reimagining of the former Formula 1 layout in Adelaide, featuring some of its most important sections, including Stag Corner, Rundle Road, Brewery Bend and Dequetteville Terrace back to life.
The 2027 MotoGP Australian Grand Prix is scheduled for the weekend of November 12, with only one race left in the calendar after that, the one in Spain. For the record, the 2027 MotoGP has no less than 22 races planned, the same as this year's season.

Cadillac Quietly Updates 2027 Escalade U.S. Pricing
12 photos
Photo: Cadillac
Cadillac phased out the 2026 Escalade to make room for the 2027 model year. The most affordable variant now starts at $102,700, which is $10,600 over the price of the most affordable variant last year. However, it does make sense, because the automaker discontinued the base Escalade for both standard and long-wheelbase variants.
This means that the lineup now starts with the 2WD Luxury trim. With fees and taxes included, it is a $105,595 deal. For the money, customers get the luxury SUV equipped with the huge 55-inch Horizon Display, stretching from pillar to pillar, offered as standard.
A head-up display and the Power SkyGlass roof are also on the menu, along with the AKG Studio 21-speaker audio system. The driver and front passenger sit in front bucket seats with 12-way power adjustment, offered as standard for the Luxury, Premium Luxury and Sport models.
Furthermore, their SUV is equipped with the Magnetic Ride Control, an Electronic Limited-Slip Differential (eLSD), and rides on 22-inch nine-spoke alloy wheels with a polished finish.
Photo: Cadillac The SUV is powered by the 6.2-liter engine, which produces 420 horsepower and 460 pound-feet of torque. A ten-speed automatic transmission puts the power down through the rear wheels in the base-trim model, or through all four corners if the buyer is willing to pay $3,000 more.
Upper the range sits the Escalade Sport 4WD, which kicks off at $109,195. For the extra money, it gets Gloss Black bodyside moldings with matching Gloss Black roof-mounted side rails. This variant rides on 22-inch alloy wheels with Dark Android and Low Gloss Finish.
The Escalade Platinum Luxury starts at $127,095 and adds the Platinum interior trim, power open-and-close doors, and the 38-speaker AKG Studio Reference sound system with Dolby Atmos. The powertrain remains unchanged.
The Platinum Sport sits at the top of the non-V range and can be purchased for a starting price of $127,595. Power-retractable assist steps with LED perimeter lighting and 22-inch 18-Spoke alloy wheels with After Midnight finish are part of the plan.
Photo: Cadillac New for 2027 is the Sandstone paint, while the Magnus Metal Frost and Aegean Stone are discontinued. The Cadillac Digital Key app is added (though it requires an over-the-air update to function), and trailer tire pressure monitoring is newly available. The Onyx Lite appearance package is now offered on Sport models.
Cadillac dropped the performance air intake, the Interior Protection package, all-weather floor mats, and removed the Onyx Lite package from the Escalade-V. Speaking of which, the range-topping Escalade starts at $172,195. For the money, customers get the 6.2-liter supercharged V8, which pumps out 682 horsepower and 653 pound-feet of torque.
A special-edition 2027 Cadillac Escalade-V 125th Anniversary Collector Series debuts with carbon fiber exterior accents, Santorini Blue stitching and expectedly, a higher price tag: $239,000. General Motors will only build 252 such examples.

A True Must See! Sidewinder Drops a Hardshell Camper With Sidecar Mounting for Motorcyclists
14 photos
Photo: Sidewinder Campers
For the longest time, motorcyclists had a hard time tapping into glamping mainly because there are too few campers out there that are light enough to hitch up to a motorcycle. Those that do exist and onto which we've shed light before are often pop-up solutions with soft shells. Well, one team has done it, giving birth to a lineup of hardshell campers aimed at steel steed lovers out there.
The name is Sidewinder, and if it weren’t for a Facebook ad, I would have never found out about this crew; they’re that obscure and under-the-radar, so to speak. As to what makes this crew so special, well, you clearly picked up on the fact that they craft campers for motorcycles, but how they do it and what they give rise to is clearly worth your attention.
Sidewinder breaks the mold of traditional bike campers in two ways. The first is that they give rise to a hardwall solution, and the second is by the positioning of those campers: they mount them in a sidecar position and are not towed along like you’d expect. I’m guessing you’re reading this BECAUSE of the main image you spotted.
Photo: Time Out Trailers, Inc. Overall, Sidewinder manufactures several options for bikers to tap into, but it’s the Pygmy that stands as the smallest (7 ft long, 4 ft wide) of the bunch, a proverbial flagship, so to speak, one that displays the bare bones that this brand has to offer rather than a frilled-out one. That’s also the RVing solution we’ll be tapping into today.
Now, as the smallest solution, Sidewinder crafts a camper that clearly weighs very little as it’s designed to be used in conjunction with a vehicle that is not known for its towing prowess. How little? How does 350 lbs (159 kg) sound?
Sure, it’s not as light as some softshell options out there, but it’s still good enough for some stronger bikes. Just keep in mind that because of how the camper is mounted to the frame, stresses are going to be a bit different, so a specialized frame is also called upon to mount these puppies to your ride.
Photo: Sidewinder Campers According to Sidewinder, this mounting system is good for cruise, adventure, and touring bikes. Grab your gear because the world just got a whole lot bigger.
Oh, and according to images on the manufacturer’s website, these sidecar campers can even be operated while there’s someone inside. Clearly, you’ll want to stick to tarmac as you do, but that is wild, nonetheless.
What we don’t know is the GVWR of the Pygmy, or any other camper spotted on Sidewinder’s website. I’ll be sure to update this article once I have that information.
This weight is granted by the way the Pygmy is completed which is a blend between wood, composite, and good old steel, birthing a rigid camper that can suit the needs of up to two guests and does so in a fashion very similar to teardrop campers, even going as far as being equipped with off-grid features.
Photo: Sidewinder Campers Given the compact footprint , space is clearly limited and the Pygmy is set up in a wagon-like arrangement, with spaces and features set up in a straight line. The front of the unit is reserved for nothing more than a space where the two owners have a place to rest their head, along with a water tank and battery underneath the floor, and at the rear, the galley block. Yes, this one has a kitchen too.
Honestly, what more could you want? It can even handle a solar panel, AC system, roof-rack, awning, and so much more. I can’t wait to find out the GVWR of this unique and about-damn-time option for riders. Insulated walls also help keep us exploring into a bit of the colder season; grab a good heater.
After you’ve made it to camp, wherever that may be, you’ll kick out a couple of stabilizer legs, turn on the solar panel and pump, unfurl your awning and set up the dining area or lounge, and finally, pop the rear hatch so that you can grab a cold drink, cook up dinner, and wash your hands.
Photo: Sidewinder Campers You may be asking where the dining set came from, but you probably figured out that it was probably stuffed inside the camper. Yet, there is more storage available underneath the floor, accessible from outside; ample space for gear and other systems. Sidewinder even shows off the Pygmy with an outside shower mounted to the side of the camper.
Keep in mind that the interior of the Pygmy offers a total of just four feet in height to work with, so you clearly won't be standing up inside this one, but for reading a book, escaping bad weather, resting, and cuddling, it’s perfect.
As for the question on our mind: How much can we expect to drop on a Pygmy? Well, for the time being, the Sidewinder doesn't showcase price for this unit and urges owners to simply reach out to them directly for a quote.
Photo: Sidewinder Campers However, some sources mention that their pricing starts somewhere around $10K (€9,000) for the smallest models, so we can take that into consideration since this is the smallest model this crew offers. Would you rock a Pygmy ?
Keep in mind one thing as you explore what you see here today, and it’s that Sidewinder offers very limited images of a Pygmy, so some are of other solutions from this brand, but there’s no doubt that the Pygmy can be just as equipped as some of the larger ones. Nothing changes much across the classes expect size and weight, of course.

C8 Chevy Corvette ZR1 Races Ford Mustang Dark Horse, Someone Gets Rolled, Though Not By Much
12 photos
Photo: Import 2 Race / YouTube
Over the past few weeks, we have been thinking that it’s already been a decidedly long time since the good folks over at the racing-focused ' Import 2 Race ' channel on YouTube have not yet returned to their traditional venue - Island Dragway in Great Meadows, New Jersey.
Instead, they still have a passion for roll races. Instead of the feisty quarter-mile dragstrip skirmishes, we have gotten a treasure trove of 65-mph roll race battles, with all the high-speed ‘drama’ happening at the legendary Pocono Raceway , a 2.5-mile tri-oval track in Blakeslee, Pennsylvania. Well, this time around, the videographer makes a change of scenery.
So, they’re still not back at Island Dragway, but at least they are coming closer to home – they were on point for a quick stint at the 2026 Sunday Funday Mod2Fame event, which took place at an airport in Sullivan County, New York. It’s a 45-mph roll race showcase, on this occasion, as the airport runway isn’t like the massive Pocono Raceway
No worries, though, as the protagonists compensate: on one side is a crimson Ford Mustang Dark Horse of the S650 generation, rocking the iconic 5.0-liter Coyote V8 with 500 horsepower on tap. Its opponent, however, is a true supercar: the black menace is the C8 iteration Chevrolet Corvette ZR1, packing a brand-new 5.5-liter twin-turbo V8 and no less than 1,064 horsepower, which is more than twice the Dark Horse’s oomph.
Well, under such circumstances, it’s pretty clear that everyone knew the outcome in advance. However, one should always expect the unexpected when drag or roll races are involved, so let’s check out the outcome together. Hint: one car finishes up in front of the other by merely a car length, which is quite unexpected, indeed.
Anyway, as far as Ford is concerned, they’re not worried about the rivalry with Chevrolet anymore because the Camaro is retired, and it’s going to take a while before General Motors puts it back into production – sometime next year at the earliest, coming back on the same underpinnings as the next-generation Cadillac CT5 and an upcoming Buick sedan.
The C8 Chevrolet Corvette , meanwhile, has its work cut out for it because it has become truly expensive – almost like a European mid-engine sports car. Truthfully, it also has cool things to show for the money, like the mid-engine setup, the all-new 6.7-liter naturally aspirated V8 packing 535 hp and 520 lb-ft of torque for the base Stingray and the returning Grand Sport, or the 721-hp Grand Sport X performance hybrid that has replaced the E-Ray starting with the 2027 model year, among other things.
As for the Mustang, it has the 795-hp Dark Horse SC just waiting around the corner for Stellantis to bring back the Hellcat V8 into the latest Charger to complete the Hemi resurrection. Cool, right?

1969 GTO "Judge" Rocks 428 V8 and 4-Speed, Owner Let It Go After 30 Years Because Wife Said So
28 photos
Photo: YouTube/Kionion Classic's
When Pontiac unleashed the GTO for the 1964 model year, it sparked the golden era of American muscle by defying General Motors corporate edicts. Conceived by John DeLorean, Bill Collins, and Russ Gee as an option package on the intermediate LeMans before becoming a standalone model in 1966, the moniker spanned five distinct generations.
Production of the nameplate ran continuously from 1964 to 1974 across four iterations, before returning from 2004 to 2006 as a fifth-generation coupe built by Holden in Australia. However, the true GTO line began in 1966 and ended with the final 1971 model-year example assembled. After that, the “GTO” reverted to an optional package for the Le Mans (and LeMans Sport), before ending as an upgrade for the compact Pontiac Ventura (the PMD counterpart to the Chevrolet Nova).
Before the 1970 model year lifted General Motors displacement caps on intermediates, the GTO relied exclusively on two motors (never overlapping in their availability timeframe): the high-output 389-cubic-inch V8 was the primordial muscle for the GTO, before being phased out at the end of ’66, in favor of the 400-incher.
From 1964 to 1966, the 389 V8 dominated the streets, offered with either a single four-barrel carburetor or the legendary Tri-Power setup featuring three two-barrel Rochester carburetors rated at up to 360 hp. Following a corporate ban on multiple carburetors after 1966 on all General Motors passenger cars except the Chevrolet Corvette, Pontiac enlarged the 389 to 400 cubic inches.
Photo: YouTube/Kionion Classic's That 400 V8 carried the GTO from 1967 through 1969 in base, economy two-barrel, High Output, and Ram Air configurations, culminating in the 370-hp Ram Air IV. At the exact same time in 1967, Pontiac bored the 421 V8 out to 428 cubic inches (7.0 liters) to replace the retired 421 Tri-Power in full-size Catalina, Executive, Bonneville, and Grand Prix models.
Because of General Motors displacement limits, the short-lived 428 V8 was never factory-installed in a GTO before vanishing after its final year in 1969. In its swan song season, the 428 V8 utilized a 4.125-inch bore and a 4.00-inch stroke alongside a revised pearlite malleable iron crankshaft marked with an N casting.
Equipped with a single four-barrel Rochester Quadrajet carburetor and a 10.5:1 compression ratio, the standard 1969 Pontiac 428 V8 delivered 360 hp at 4,600 rpm and 472 lb-ft of torque at 3,200 rpm, plus a 370-hp rating in the Grand Prix. Stepping up to the 428 High Output variant with 10.75:1 compression unlocked 390 hp at 5,200 rpm and 465 lb-ft of torque at 3,400 rpm.
Photo: YouTube/Kionion Classic's It was a lot of muscle, and the GTO – by definition the quintessential high-performer of the division – would have deserved to carry that almighty engine in full. While Pontiac never bolted a 428 into a GTO on the assembly line, one gearhead decided to right that historical wrong with a build of his own. You can admire the car in the video below, with all its pros and cons.
The 1969 Pontiac GTO featured by Adam Kinion on the Kinion Classic's YouTube channel brings that exact combination to life. Listed through the Kinion Auto Sales and Service dealership in Clarence, Iowa, at an asking price of $44,900, this two-door hardtop carries 87,265 miles on the odometer. The car was owned for nearly 30 years by the best friend of Adam father, Dale Kinion.
Back in 1991, Dale Kinion sold his friend a genuine Carousel Red GTO Judge, which sat alongside this blue 1969 coupe for nearly three decades. When the owner's wife recently suggested that one of the two Pontiacs needed to go, he offered the blue 1969 GTO directly to Adam. (Sidenote: I’m no marriage counselor, but I imagine that man must love his spouse to the moon end of the galaxy - and back).
Photo: YouTube/Kionion Classic's Although dressed as a Judge tribute with fender decals, side stripes, and a rear airfoil, its Pontiac Historical Services invoice confirms it left the Baltimore plant in February 1969 as a true Ram Air car.
Delivered new to Johnson Pontiac in Colorado Springs, Colorado, with a factory 400-cubic-inch four-barrel Ram Air V8, a close-ratio 4-speed manual transmission, a Safe-T-Track rear axle, concealed headlamps, Rally II wheels, power steering, and a console, the coupe now houses a built 428 V8.
The previous long-time owner invested close to 12,000 into building the 428-cubic-inch powerplant, fitting an aluminum intake manifold while retaining the stock exhaust manifolds, the factory Ram Air air cleaner assembly with its foam hood seal, a newer radiator, and a fresh battery and alternator.
Photo: YouTube/Kionion Classic's Whereas a factory 428 V8 produced anywhere between 360 hp or 390 hp in 1969, the custom-built 428 inside this GTO pairs its bored-and-honed internals and aluminum intake with the 4-speed manual gearbox to outrun standard 396 or 454 street machines. Adam Kinion notes during his road test that the engine is cold-blooded and stalls a couple of times while below operating temperature.
It’s a minor carburetor choke quirk common to vintage muscle cars, that vanishes once warmed up on the open Iowa highway. During the walkaround, the dealer initially states the car has power disc brakes, but corrects himself after opening the hood and inspecting the master cylinder, confirming it relies on manual four-wheel drum brakes that stop with surprising authority.
Wearing a restoration completed roughly 25 years ago, the blue exterior remains solid underneath, with clean doors, fenders, hood, and trunk floor, complemented by PMD Rally II wheels wrapped in raised-white-letter BFGoodrich Radial T/A tires and rear quarter glass decals reading “The Heartbeat Stops Here.”
Photo: YouTube/Kionion Classic's The YouTuber points out every flaw on the quarter-century-old finish. On the upper right-side rear quarter panel near the C-pillar and quarter window, a faint seam line is visible under direct shop lighting where a replacement panel was spliced and leaded in. Lower down on that same passenger-side quarter panel, just behind the door gap, the metal exhibits minor surface waves from an old patch repair, while the chrome bumpers display fine scratches.
Inside the cabin, the blue vinyl bucket seats, center console, wood-rimmed PMD steering wheel, headliner, visors, sail panels, door jambs, and sill plates present in remarkably clean condition. However, the plastic seatback shells on the front buckets and the green-tinged lower armrest pads on the doors show noticeable paint fading from age.
Photo: YouTube/Kionion Classic's On the dashboard, the speedometer, tachometer, fuel, oil pressure, and temperature gauges all function properly alongside the radio, heater blower, wipers, turn signals, and cigarette lighter, leaving the non-operational horn as the lone electrical hiccup. It’s probably something a car nut will let slide, considering this Judge tribute of sorts isn’t going to be anyone’s daily driver (although it could serve as one without problems – fuel economy not withstanding).
Complete with its original build sheet, owner's manual, and documentation packet, this $44,900 428-powered 1969 GTO stands as the historic repair for a corporate decision that denied the greatest muscle car of the sixties the arsenal to tackle any Hemi Mopar, Boss Mustang , or even big-block Chevys, Olds, or Buicks.

Amflow, the electric bicycle brand that burst onto the scene with some of the most powerful and lightweight electric mountain bikes on the market, is expanding its lineup with two major releases. The company has announced global availability of its new Amflow TL Carbon, while also bringing its removable-battery Amflow PR Carbon series to the US for the first time.
Both models are powered by the latest Avinox mid-drive motor systems, which have quickly earned a reputation for delivering impressive power in surprisingly compact packages.
The biggest departure from Amflow’s roots is the new TL Carbon, which takes the company’s high-performance mountain biking DNA and applies it to a more versatile SUV-style electric bike. While less common in the US (ironically), SUV-style e-bikes are essentially a hybrid electric bicycle designed to act as an all-in-one, “do-it-all” vehicle combining the rugged build and off-road capability of an electric mountain bike with the practical, everyday utility of a city or trekking bike.
Rather than focusing exclusively on technical trails and aggressive mountain biking, the TL Carbon is designed to handle everything from daily commuting to touring and off-road adventures. And with Avinox’s RS800 battery featuring 800Wh of capacity, it’s got plenty of energy on board for diverse adventures.
Advertisement - scroll for more content
The full-suspension bike uses the Avinox M2 motor, delivering up to 125 Nm of torque, which should provide more than enough grunt for steep climbs, heavy loads, and just about anything else riders can throw at it.
Avinox e-bike drive systems are known for many things, but chief among them is the extremely high power and torque they offer , eclipsing most other mid-drive motor systems on the market.
Despite that power and versatility, the TL Carbon weighs as little as 22.6 kg (49.8 lb). It also boasts an impressive maximum total weight capacity of 200 kg (441 lb), including the bike itself, rider, and cargo carried on its front and rear racks.
That’s a compelling combination for riders who want the performance of a premium electric mountain bike but need something practical enough to replace a car for everyday trips.
And perhaps most surprisingly, the price isn’t completely outrageous. The Amflow TL Carbon starts at $3,899 in the US and €3,499 in Germany, positioning it competitively against premium European trekking and SUV-style e-bikes.
Meanwhile, American riders are finally getting access to the Amflow PR Carbon series, which had previously launched in other markets.
Unlike Amflow’s earlier electric mountain bikes, the PR series features a removable battery, addressing one of the biggest practical complaints about high-performance eMTBs with integrated batteries.
The new 800 Wh battery weighs just 4 kg (8.8 lb) and can be removed for convenient indoor charging or swapped for a fresh battery to extend a ride. That’s especially useful for riders who don’t have a convenient charging outlet near their bike storage area.
Amflow claims up to 158 km (98 miles) of range under ideal conditions, though that’s based on relatively gentle riding on flat pavement in Eco mode. Riders tackling technical trails with high assistance levels should expect considerably less. But any way you slice it, 800 Wh is a huge battery for eMTBs and should deliver plenty of range under most conditions.
The standard PR Carbon uses the Avinox M2 motor with up to 125 Nm of torque, while the higher-end PR Carbon Pro upgrades to the more powerful Avinox M2S motor, producing up to 150 Nm of torque.
In the US, the PR Carbon starts at $4,999, while the PR Carbon Pro commands $6,799. European pricing starts at €4,499 and €5,899, respectively, based on German pricing.
All three bikes are available beginning today through ⁠Amflow’s official website and its network of authorized dealers. In the US, both models generally arrive as Class 1 e-bikes (no throttle) with a top speed of 20 mph (32 km/h), though Amflow models can typically be unlocked to Class 3 performance with a top speed of 28 mph (45 km/h).
Electrek’s Take
Amflow has been one of the more interesting brands to watch in the premium e-bike space, largely because of how aggressively it has pushed the boundaries of motor performance and bike weight.
But these latest releases show that the company is thinking beyond simply building increasingly powerful electric mountain bikes.
The TL Carbon is particularly interesting to me because it brings that impressive Avinox performance to a more practical platform. As someone who spends a minority of my riding time in the dirt, Amflow suddenly looks a lot more interesting to me, personally. Not everyone needs a dedicated eMTB, but plenty of riders would appreciate a lightweight, powerful, well-equipped electric bike that can handle both weekday commuting and weekend adventures.
And the PR Carbon’s removable battery is a welcome development, especially as the industry continues to recognize that convenience and serviceability matter just as much as outright performance.
With the Avinox ecosystem continuing to expand across more bike brands and categories, Amflow is also facing increasing competition from other manufacturers using the same impressive motors. That makes it all the more important for the brand to differentiate itself through thoughtful bike design, not just headline-grabbing power figures.

This Is How NASA's Artemis III Will Test the Blue Origin Blue Moon Lander in Earth Orbit
10 photos
Photo: NASA
It's been a big week for American space agency NASA and all those interested in space exploration, as administrator Jared Isaacman and a bunch of other officials announced new details of the accelerated Artemis program. Among the details we learned was fresh info on how the third mission of the program, scheduled for next year, will unfold.
NASA makes no secret of the fact that this will be the most complex mission it has ever undertaken, despite the fact that none of the spacecraft and people involved would go further than Earth orbit.
For the first time in history, though, three different launch rockets and three different spacecraft will be involved in the mission, whose main goal is to test and validate the landers being constructed by private space companies SpaceX and Blue Origin.
NASA already provided us a glimpse of what to expect from Artemis III earlier this year, but since that time the plans have been altered a bit, and new, previously unknown details have surfaced.
As said, Artemis III will see four astronauts (Randy Bresnik, Frank Rubio, Andre Douglas, and Luca Parmitano) climb aboard the Orion spacecraft and head to orbit where they'll dock and otherwise test two privately made landers. We'll give each of these landers their own story, so we can make better sense of them.
Photo: NASA/Blue Origin I'll start with the Blue Origin lander, the one officially called the Blue Moon Mark 2 Alpha, for the simple reason that this will be the first piece of hardware to fly as part of the Artemis III mission.
Sent to Earth orbit by Blue Origin's New Glenn rocket, the Mark 2 will park itself some 273 miles (439 km) from the surface of the planet. Technically speaking, it can stay up there, waiting for the astronauts to arrive, for about 30 days.
NASA, however, hopes things will go a little smoother, and only a few days after the launch of the Blue Moon, the four astronauts should be transported into orbit by the Space Launch System (SLS) rocket and the Orion spacecraft.
Once free of Earth's gravitational pull, the Orion will follow an elliptical orbit and, aided by the service module, will adjust its position to transition to a circular orbit 345 miles (555 km) above Earth. From there, further adjustments would be needed so that it can get in position for hook-up with the Blue Moon.
Photo: Blue Origin The entire Artemis III mission is expected to last for 14 days, and the crew will spend the first two days checking out the Orion and getting in shape for the kiss with the lander. Then, if everything goes according to plan, the Orion and the Blue Moon will connect themselves together.
Over the next couple of days following the hookup, two astronauts will transfer into the lander and begin putting it through its paces, looking to test the guidance systems, communications, operational procedures, cabin environment, controls, and life-support systems, among others.
Although a test article by trade, the Blue Moon lander will be equipped with many of the avionics, software, flight-control systems, crew-cabin technologies, and life-support functions the actual lander will use, making the test even more important.
Once the two days of testing are up, the Orion will undock from the Blue Origin lander and position itself for the second docking maneuver, this time the one with the SpaceX Starship lander. This time, the crew won't board the ship, and the time spent attached to the Starship will be much shorter.
Photo: Blue Origin NASA said at the end of last week that it hasn't decided yet on what lander will be used for the Artemis IV Moon landing coming in 2028. Should it pick the Blue Moon, here's what we can expect from it.
To support the Moon landing, Blue Origin will launch into Earth orbit three transfer stages, as well as the lander itself. Once linked together, the stack would embark on a journey that will eventually take the Mark 2 into an elliptical polar orbit around the Moon.
The crew-carrying Orion would then join it there, and, once docked, two astronauts would move over to the lander to begin their descent to the surface. Once their mission down there is complete, they would climb back on board the Blue Moon and be transported to the Orion, which would then bring them all back home.
Blue Origin is in a pretty advanced stage of development with the Blue Moon, and it has recently committed to adding new human-in-the-loop testing and hardware readiness milestones to make sure everything is ready in time for the Moon landing.
Separately, Jeff Bezos' space company is also working on a cargo version of the lander, which will be used to help NASA build the permanent Moon Base on the planet's natural satellite. We'll keep an eye on that and report back once we know more.
